fact_text: A GEP employment visa requires a confirmed job offer and is granted for a specific employer and role; it is not a free-standing right to work, so it is effectively tied to the sponsoring employer.
evidence_quote: the applicant has a confirmed offer of employment and is employed in a job relevant to his academic qualifications or work experience that cannot be readily taken up by the local work force

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a work visa lets you work anywhere in Hong Kong. Actually: the GEP visa is granted against one confirmed employer/role and depends on that job continuing. Action: if the employee changes employer, a fresh visa application is required.

fact_text: A third-country national needs a visa or entry permit to take up employment in Hong Kong; entering as a visitor does not permit starting work while an application is pending.
evidence_quote: unless a person has the right of abode or right to land in the HKSAR, he/she requires a visa/entry permit to work in the HKSAR

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you can land on a visitor pass and begin work while the employment visa is processed. Actually: without right of abode/right to land you must hold the visa/entry permit before working. Action: do not start work until the GEP visa is granted.

fact_text: A spouse/eligible partner and unmarried children under 18 admitted as GEP dependants are permitted to take up employment or study in Hong Kong without a separate work visa.
evidence_quote: These dependants are not prohibited from taking up employment or studies in the HKSAR under the existing policy.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: an accompanying spouse on a dependant visa cannot work. Actually: GEP dependants are not prohibited from taking up employment or study. Action: the spouse can accept a job in Hong Kong on the dependant visa without applying for their own employment visa.

entity_title: GEP processing ~four weeks after complete file
fact_text: Immigration normally takes about four weeks to process a GEP application, but the clock only starts once ALL required documents and the fee have been received.
evidence_quote: it normally takes four weeks upon receipt of all the required documents and the relevant application fee

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the four-week processing time runs from the date you submit. Actually: it runs only from receipt of a COMPLETE file plus fee; a missing document resets the start. Action: assemble every required document before filing to avoid restarting the four-week window.

entity_title: TTPS needs no job offer to apply
fact_text: Unlike the GEP, the Top Talent Pass Scheme lets high-income earners and top-university graduates enter Hong Kong without a job offer, granting 24 or 36 months' stay with no employer condition.
evidence_quote: Persons who wish to apply to enter the HKSAR under the TTPS are not required to have secured an offer of employment in the HKSAR upon application.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: every Hong Kong work route needs a sponsoring employer. Actually: TTPS entrants get an open, employer-agnostic stay of 24-36 months with no job offer required. Action: an eligible relocatee can enter on TTPS and then take up or change employment freely.

entity_title: HK Identity Card registration is mandatory
fact_text: Anyone aged 11+ residing in Hong Kong must register for a Hong Kong Identity Card; only those permitted to stay 180 days or less are exempt, so a relocated professional on a work visa must obtain an HKID.
evidence_quote: all residents of Hong Kong aged 11 or above are required to register for an identity card, except those who have been exempted

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the work visa in the passport is all the ID you need. Actually: residents aged 11+ must register for a HK Identity Card; only stays of 180 days or less are exempt. Action: book a Registration of Persons Office appointment and register for the HKID promptly after arrival.

fact_text: Hong Kong salaries tax applies only to income arising in or derived from Hong Kong employment, offices and pension - it is territorial, not worldwide.
evidence_quote: Salaries tax is chargeable on most but not all of the income from employment, offices and pension arising in or derived from Hong Kong.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: Hong Kong taxes your worldwide income like many home countries. Actually: salaries tax is territorial - only income arising in or derived from Hong Kong is chargeable. Action: foreign-source income unconnected to the HK job is generally outside HK salaries tax.

entity_title: No PAYE withholding - you file and pay
fact_text: Hong Kong has no monthly PAYE withholding of salaries tax; the employee files a tax return and pays after receiving a notice of assessment, and must proactively notify the IRD if no return is issued.
evidence_quote: If you do not receive a tax return you should notify the Inland Revenue Department that your income could be chargeable to tax.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: tax is deducted from each pay cheque as in most PAYE countries. Actually: HK has no salary withholding - you file a return and pay after assessment, and must notify IRD if no return arrives. Action: budget/reserve cash for the tax bill and provisional tax rather than expecting payroll deductions.

fact_text: Employers must enrol qualifying employees aged 18-64 employed for 60 days or more into an MPF scheme within the first 60 days of employment.
evidence_quote: in an MPF scheme within the first 60 days of their employment.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: pension enrolment is optional or the employee arranges it. Actually: the employer is legally required to enrol a qualifying employee in an MPF scheme within the first 60 days of employment. Action: confirm the employer has enrolled you before day 60.

entity_title: MPF exemption for first 13 months / overseas scheme
fact_text: Employees entering Hong Kong for employment for not more than 13 months, or who are members of a retirement scheme outside Hong Kong, are exempt persons under the MPF System.
evidence_quote: for the purpose of employment (1) for not more than 13 months or (2) who are members of a retirement scheme of a place outside Hong Kong

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: every worker must join MPF from day one. Actually: an expatriate entering for 13 months or less, or already in a home-country retirement scheme, is an exempt person. Action: if a short-term assignment is later extended past 13 months, the employer must enrol you within 60 days of the exemption ending.

entity_title: MPF is 5% from employee and 5% from employer
fact_text: Both employee and employer must each contribute 5% of the employee's relevant income to the employee's MPF account, subject to statutory minimum and maximum income levels.
evidence_quote: Employees and employers are both required to make mandatory contributions of 5% of the employee’s relevant income into the employee’s MPF account

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: MPF is a single deduction or a foreign-style payroll tax. Actually: it is 5% from the employee plus a separate 5% funded by the employer, each capped at HK$1,500/month for income above HK$30,000. Action: expect a 5% deduction from pay in addition to the employer's own 5%.

entity_title: Direct issue of HK licence without a test
fact_text: Holders of a valid full driving licence issued by a country/place listed in Schedule 4 of Cap. 374B can apply for direct issue of a Hong Kong full driving licence without taking a driving test.
evidence_quote: Apply for direct issue of a full driving licence without test

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you must re-sit a driving test to drive in Hong Kong. Actually: if your full licence is from a country/place listed in Schedule 4 of Cap. 374B you can get a HK full licence by direct issue without a test. Action: check the Schedule 4 list and apply for direct issue before your home licence lapses.
